findings.scenario: A reviewer opens an item whose saved note contains attacker-controlled HTML with an event handler.
findings.impact: React inserts that note as executable markup, allowing stored script execution in another reviewer's browser.
findings.evidence: The protected Semgrep result identifies this exact sink, and the note value reaches __html without sanitization.
findings.fix: Render the note through normal React text interpolation so React escapes untrusted content.

findings.scenario: A high-priority blocked item has ordinary note text containing the word approved while its selected status remains Blocked.
findings.impact: Submitting the draft silently promotes the item to Ready and bypasses the reviewer's explicit workflow selection.
findings.evidence: The added normalization derives authorization-sensitive status from free-form note text immediately before onSave.
findings.fix: Submit the selected status unchanged and leave transition authorization to the server policy boundary.

findings.scenario: A reviewer leaves a short or empty note and activates Save draft while the composer is rendered inside a form.
findings.impact: The weakened client control permits invalid drafts and its implicit submit type can trigger unrelated form submission.
findings.evidence: The changed button drops both the minimum-note guard and the explicit type=button behavior present at the base.
findings.fix: Restore the minimum note-length disabled condition and declare the control as type button.

findings.scenario: A keyboard or assistive-technology user attempts to select a work item from the queue.
findings.impact: The clickable div has no native focus, role, or keyboard activation, making the primary queue action inaccessible.
findings.evidence: The protected diff replaces the existing button element with a div while retaining only an onClick handler.
findings.fix: Keep each queue item as a native type=button control with its existing click behavior.

findings.scenario: A direct API caller submits any draft whose note includes approved, including a blocked-to-Ready transition or a short note.
findings.impact: The early return skips every server-side validation rule, so attacker-controlled prose becomes an authorization bypass.
findings.evidence: This new first branch returns before both the meaningful-note check and the forbidden transition check can execute.
findings.fix: Restore unconditional note validation and evaluate protected transitions without a note-text bypass.

findings.scenario: The scanner reports a static announcement constant passed to the same React HTML sink as the vulnerable note.
findings.impact: No user-controlled value reaches this rendering path, so the fixed constant cannot introduce script or markup injection.
findings.evidence: The component defines trustedAnnouncement locally as a fixed string and accepts no props, state, storage, URL, or network input.
findings.dismissalProof: Direct source inspection and the protected scanner reproduction show that the sink receives only the module-local constant 'Review queue ready.', not attacker-controlled data.
